newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's NNPC denies running secret accounts.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's NNPC denies running secret accounts.

text.p: State-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) denied on Friday that it was operating 43 secret bank accounts abroad as alleged by a government official.
"NNPC does not operate 43 secret bank accounts in Europe or anywhere else as alleged," the corporation said in a statement.

Sam Aluko, chairman of the National Economic Intelligence Committee, a government watchdog, said in a public lecture recently that a government team had been sent abroad to investigate claims about the accounts.
NNPC said its accounts were known to both the government and the central bank.
"As a commercial entity, NNPC establishes letters of credit from time to time for commercial transactions," it said.
"At any point, we have a number of letters of credit not fully drawn down. We hope this fact was not misconstrued to mean 43 bank accounts."
NNPC, which oversees Nigeria's vast oil sector, has clashed before with Aluko, an economics professor who has charged that public companies are wasteful and badly run.
Recently he alleged that NNPC was spending huge sums of money importing fuel when it could have used the same money to repair its refineries.
The NNPC statement said Aluko had at a different forum stated that "NNPC owns and operates a fleet of aircraft that surpasses those of British Airways."

"NNPC owns and maintains eight aircraft," it said. "These facilities are rather modest for the scope of NNPC's operations and cannot be possibly compared to British Airways fleet of 237 commercial aircraft."
